paragraphs: Friend, the disciples walked up with a question about the PAST: who sinned? Jesus answered, 'Neither this man nor his parents sinned, but this happened so that the works of God would be displayed in him.' (John 9:3) He turned them from looking back for someone to blame to looking at the work of God right in front of them. So when something hard in your life has you digging for the reason, hear that, baker.

Now look at what the man did when the pressure came. His neighbors argued about him, the Pharisees questioned him twice, and his parents slid the question right back to him. He didn't have a perfect answer for every question, and he said so. He held onto the one thing he did know: 'I was blind, but now I see!' (John 9:25) You don't need to win every argument to tell the truth about what Jesus has done for you, friend.

Then Jesus found him, and the man said, 'Lord, I believe,' and he worshiped Him. (John 9:38) The ones who claimed they could see were the ones whose guilt remained, because Jesus said, 'But since you claim you can see, your guilt remains.' (John 9:41) The man who knew he needed light got it, and the ones sure they didn't need it stayed in the dark. So come to Jesus the way that man did, baker, with your hands open and nothing to prove.
